rv.q: The show has its problems, some inherent in the range of Weill's music, and a few that seem to be almost willfully wrong-headed choices by director Harold Prince and author Alfred Uhry.

That wounding impulse to abnegate both the love itself and the pain that comes with denial colors every scene of “LoveMusik,” an uneven but fascinating portrait of the corrosive relationship between Weill and his wife Lotte Lenya.
Any show, no matter how uneven, that includes such a moment can be forgiven much.
I found LoveMusik itself a strangely tired show—a missed opportunity to achieve something original and genuinely Brechtian with Kurt Weill's music and the story of the Weill-Lenya marriage.
The show is daring, indeed, but considering all the talent involved ultimately disappointing and rarely moving.

tn.cat: Best Featured Actor in a Musical

cn.t: Critics are divided on this Weill-Lenya bio-musical: most praise the luminous lead performances by Cerveris and Murphy and Prince's moody direction, but find the show itself sluggish and tedious despite its ambitious, grown-up approach.
